root_decision: Do not add new prefetch/KV/stop risks now; retain measured short-request gains and honestly report long-output regression. No speed benefit claimed for this untested design.
proposal: First20 actual decode forwards use block2, later block4; prefill excluded from counter

evidence.finding: prefill_interval controls both get_prealloc_size and get_num_loops.
Schedule with KV preallocation precedes loop_count selection; _send_next_inputs_impl sends the complete block to executor.
Prefetch begins before receiving current block final output; mutating global interval on response token20 can act one block late.

safe_design_conditions: Restrict initial scope to one active sequence; maintain per-sequence issued decode-forward budget, not returned token count.
Atomically decide block length and enough KV preallocation at InputsMaker creation/submission boundary; never mutate a running worker block.
Count prefill separately; first20 decode forwards means ten2-forward blocks, followed by4-forward blocks.
Alternative always-prealloc4 plus loop_count2/4 is explicitly a preallocation change and needs its own memory/fairness assessment.
Reset sequence budget on new request/cancel/stop; prefetched old work must not leak to next request.
risks: Worker does not break its block immediately on EOS; later4-forward blocks can still delay FINISH delivery.
CounterEvent changes token arrival batching in streaming; stream/nonstream evidence cannot be pooled.
Chunk boundary changes need seeded stochastic and natural-EOS equivalence checks even when per-token stopping rules remain unchanged.
Output length18 usually remains in initial2-forward phase; long64 benefits are only a hypothesis, not a result.
required_if_revisited: Same-weight full token equality plus seeded stochastic checks
KV allocation boundary and fairness checks
Separate streaming arrival and nonstream request latency contracts
